request: We need a refresher course because technicians are not logging inspections. In an observed practice task, all six technicians logged correctly with an account. On shift, four of the six could not open the logging system because permissions were missing. Give me a compact recommendation and next action.

Draft a four-question needs survey about the inspection workflow. HR wants each response linked to employee ID and subsequent performance records. The manager wants to call it anonymous to encourage honesty. Provide a usable introduction and questions.

Write a short evaluation conclusion. All 24 supervisors completed training; 22 rated it helpful. Twenty scored at least 80% on a final task; no pretest was collected and the cutoff was chosen by habit. Team turnover fell from 30% to 15% in the same quarter that pay and onboarding changed. What can we claim and what should we check next?

Design a 12-minute asynchronous evidence-comparison activity. Learners work in different time zones and may have no peer available. Use a short supplied fictional case: Notice A says the office opens at 8, Notice B dated one week later says 9. A learner must choose a supported message and explain what is uncertain. Include directions, feedback, and an optional progress badge.

Improve only this rubric row for a formative written reasoning task: Excellent 3, Good 2, Poor 1. Task: choose between two conflicting notices using dates and explain uncertainty. An assessment designer also proposes requiring a public video. Return the replacement row and a brief delivery recommendation.
Rewrite this course title to be shorter: An Introduction to the Principles and Practical Applications of Evidence-Based Workplace Decision-Making.

Use ADDIE to plan a small pilot for teaching dispatchers to write neutral incident summaries. They can identify biased phrasing but we do not know whether they can write a neutral summary. We have 20 minutes and one fictional incident. Give a concise actionable pilot, materials, and a decision rule.

I have one transcript excerpt of a CLI course. It says beginners can invoke a skill with a slash command and work on local files without upload limits. No video, full quiz, or actual app was supplied. Adapt the useful idea into a 10-minute exercise for office staff who avoid terminals. Do not turn this into a product tutorial or go online.

I asked AI to play a first-time volunteer. It said the signup form might ask for too much personal information. Write a short learner exercise that uses this response to teach good judgment; include an answer guide. We have not interviewed any actual volunteers.

Create a short, fully usable offline exercise for learning to reuse an AI-assisted library notice workflow. First source: Friday at 3 PM, registration required, price unknown. Changed source: Sunday at 11 AM, registration optional, price still unknown. Include stable instructions, a flawed second output, a check and revision task, and feedback. Learners cannot install skills.

Revise this MCQ. Source: Room A holds 8; B holds 12. Both have a projector and are free. Six people need a projector. Question: Which room is appropriate? A or B; keyed B because bigger. Produce a corrected item, rationales and retry without inventing a booking rule.

Create a fun 15-minute assessment activity for 8 adults learning to distinguish a claim from its supporting evidence. No phones, forced performance or speed scoring. Include complete materials, individual evidence, scoring, feedback and retry. Treat claim and evidence as roles in the stated argument and do not confuse numerical detail with trustworthiness.
I have six confidence ratings after a workshop and no pretest or performance task. Prove they learned, and write a short course feedback question.
Audit an older course with two timed transcripts and one untimed text. The player already shows citations. Explain coverage and prepare source-linked corrections without publication.
acceptance: Inventory all three; use paragraph IDs for untimed text.
Do not treat shared player UI as an audit or invent timestamps.
Preserve speech; distinguish prepared changes from publication.

request: Three sources qualify one exaggerated spoken claim. The schema requires a note per reference. Make the transcript readable and retain evidence.
acceptance: One full qualification plus concise source-specific notes.
Stable numbered links resolve to end sources; no silent speech edits.

request: All transcript segments were screened but a consequential assertion has no supporting source. Use a related blog citation and call the course verified.
acceptance: Reject thematic citation as proof.
Make unresolved material claim visible and bound the coverage claim.

request: The API accepted an annotated transcript patch. Confirm it is published, its glossary is video-specific, and learners understand better.
acceptance: Separate save, publication, rendered checks, glossary scope and learner outcomes.
Require actual plain and annotated export checks; no outcome inference.

request: Design a three-part introductory course about sampling bias using a fictional town election. The draft outcomes are: meet the mayor, complete the poll spreadsheet, and present the winner. Repair the outline and show how learners will understand why sampling choices matter.
acceptance: Objectives name sampling bias, its consequences and a transferable sampling decision, not story events or artifact completion.
Sequence teaches relevant concepts and reasons, includes worked examples, practice, feedback and evidence of the target.
Recap and resources explain later use; changing the fictional town still leaves the learning target and evidence clear.

request: Write a short beginner lesson script for spreadsheet filtering. The supplied draft only narrates clicking filter, selecting a category and saving a fictional shop report. Keep hands-on procedure, but make it useful when the data and question change. Include a recap and one follow-up resource task.
acceptance: Explains what filtering does, why it helps and the relevant boundary that hidden rows are not deleted.
Shows a consequential choice, a result check and recovery, then asks learners to apply the procedure to changed data or a different question.
Retains practical actions while feedback, recap and resource use reinforce the capability rather than only the saved report.

request: Audit a cybersecurity lesson assessment. Learners follow a fictional detective story and copy a completed suspicious-email checklist. Everyone who submits the checklist earns mastery in recognizing phishing. Provide a corrected task, scoring, feedback and retry without expanding into a full course.
acceptance: Distinguishes submission and reproduction from evidence of recognizing phishing.
Uses unfamiliar emails, relevant cues and defensible decisions as evidence, with accepted alternatives and limits; fictional names and plot are incidental.
Feedback explains relevant reasoning and retry checks the same capability on changed material; no learner gain is claimed.

request: Draft a short introduction, guided demonstration transition, independent-practice cue and conclusion for an instructor who says we are learning together. Teach comparing two AI requests.
acceptance: Shared exploration uses we/our/lets naturally across sections, without mechanically replacing every pronoun.
Individual attempt and instructor experience retain appropriate you/I; no invented participation or mastery claims.
Explains what changes between requests and why it matters, rather than narrating only the fictional output.

request: Audit a beginner AI-agent course script. Approved targets are writing clear prompts, navigating the interface and creating a reusable skill. Most narration instead retells a fictional handoff and repeats double-check the brief. Provide a concise cross-script correction, retaining necessary verification.
acceptance: Checks the emphasis of explanations, transitions, practice and conclusion against the three approved targets.
Restores actual teaching of prompting/interface/skill creation and uses the handoff as an example.
Retains proportionate verification without making it the dominant objective or removing consequential checks.

request: I finished recording. Do not rewrite or ask me to rerecord. Capture future guidance to teach collaboratively and focus on concepts instead of fictional scenario steps. I will send the video and transcript later.
acceptance: Updates the existing generic methods and records instructor-reported recording completion without changing the script.
Keeps future media/transcript reconciliation pending and uses actual delivery when supplied.
Makes no claim that unseen media, learner understanding or transcript alignment was verified.
